vocabulary.collection_rule: Pytest only collects functions whose names start with ``test_`` (or methods on classes starting with ``Test``).
vocabulary.fake_builtin_rule:
- When a test must fake a built-in function, replace it only in the
  module under test, for example
  ``monkeypatch.setattr(module, "len", fake, raising=False)``, not in
  ``builtins``. To simulate a missing optional package, use
  ``monkeypatch.setitem(sys.modules, "name", None)``.
vocabulary.load_error_patterns:
- ImportError -> verify the name actually exists in the
    target module / fix the import path.
  - SyntaxError / IndentationError -> check the working file for
    unbalanced brackets, bad indentation, stray characters from
    a previous edit.
  - NameError at module top-level -> ensure the name is
    imported / defined before it's used.
vocabulary.parse_error_hints: missing colon at end of def/if/for, unbalanced brackets/parens/quotes, mismatched indentation, accidental code-fence remnants
vocabulary.single_file_rule: Produce one ``test_*.py`` file. Do not create helper files or runner scripts.
vocabulary.stands_alone_advice:
1. A test must leave the module under test as it found it. Change
     it only through monkeypatch, which restores what it set, or
     restore it in a fixture; reloading the module in place replaces
     every function and class the later tests use. To run import-time
     code (an ``if TYPE_CHECKING:`` block, an ``except ImportError:``
     fallback), reload it in a fixture that first saves
     ``dict(module.__dict__)`` as ``saved`` and afterwards restores it
     with ``module.__dict__.clear()`` and ``module.__dict__.update(saved)``.
  2. A test must restore a library setting it changes: use the
     library's context manager (np.errstate, np.printoptions,
     xr.set_options) or save and restore the setting in a fixture.
  3. A test must not rely on the measurement's fixed random seed or on
     dask's default scheduler: seed or configure what it uses.
vocabulary.test_dependencies:
Test toolkit (always available):
  - pytest (the runner; @pytest.fixture, @pytest.mark.parametrize, pytest.raises)
  - unittest.mock (stdlib; Mock, MagicMock, patch, patch.object, sentinel)
The project's own ``import`` graph is also available (import the module under test directly). Third-party libraries beyond pytest + unittest.mock are only available if the project's ``requirements.txt`` / ``pyproject.toml`` declares them; check before importing unfamiliar names.
vocabulary.validity_rule: Allowed: the target's runtime behaviour and documented metadata (attributes, __dict__ and vars(), __name__, __doc__, annotations, inspect.signature). Forbidden: reading or analysing its source text (inspect.getsource, its file) or bytecode (__code__, dis), executing copied source, or attributing synthetic code to its source locations.
